brief: A drawer unit that is quiet to open and looks pretty on a bookshelf.

requirements.evidence: Three slide drawers (drawer:0, drawer:1, drawer:2 refs drawer:*#0,0#cut) stacked in three half-n bases at 0,0 levels 0-2, capped and joint-locked
Chose slide-style drawers (the smoothest-running pulling style offered) over hinge/swing styles, all left closed; the configurator checks fit only and cannot verify noise or smoothness in use

Compact half-width column (~191mm wide, 240mm tall) with a plain top cover, caps on all open faces and bolted joints, dressed with a small terracotta pot on top beside where books sit; aesthetics beyond neat closed furniture form cannot be verified by the configurator
Half-n footprint is shallower than a full hex cell and 240mm of stacked drawers is shelf-scale; actual shelf dimensions were not given, so fit against a specific shelf cannot be confirmed

finish.summary: A compact three-drawer tower for a bookshelf: three half-n bases stacked at 0,0 (levels 0–2), each fitted with a slide-style drawer chosen for smooth, quiet running, topped with a plain cover, all open faces capped and joints locked, and dressed with a small terracotta pot on top. check_build is clear. Quietness and shelf fit are marked partial because the configurator verifies geometry and fit only, not running noise or your shelf's dimensions.

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.

result.note: A drawer sits on the cut face of a half base: place a half base first. Half-n and half-s take any drawer style; half-e and half-w take a slide, swing or long drawer (find_sockets offers those once the half base is on). No place on the build takes this part right now. Change the build so it can (for example add the cells it needs beside or below it), then ask again. Guessing raw ops for a part with no offers rarely works.
